title: Make the reader cite earlier deliverables or decline the reading
summary: Add a reader rule: when a reading depends on something an earlier job was meant to deliver, it must cite the path or commit where that deliverable is present in the workspace, otherwise it declines (capability null, decline_reason naming the missing deliverable). The rule goes in the reading schema field descriptions in outputs.rs because reader.md is at its token budget; audience is Athena's reader agents and the users whose requests they read.

defaults_applied.how: A unit test checks the schema carries the rule; cargo test and clippy pass.
The test asserts the generated schema text states the cite-or-refuse rule, not just that a field exists.
The rule is enforced via the schema description the reader sees; the absence of runtime enforcement is recorded as prose-only.
One focused change to the reading schema descriptions plus a test.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check.
Doc comments and the decision entry are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The rule is for Athena's reader role (this prompt), not for the producer or verifier.
'Refuse the reading' means set capability to null and put the missing deliverable in decline_reason, the existing refusal path.

reader.md is at its token budget (docs/decisions.md; outputs.rs comment), so the rule lives in the schema field descriptions (doc comments on capability/decline_reason in ReadingOutput), as the urgent_reason rule does.
No runtime check that the cited path exists is added; the reader has Read/Glob to verify it itself. This is marked prose-only.

acceptance_criteria.text: The ReadingOutput doc comments in crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs state that a reading depending on an earlier job's deliverable must cite the path or commit where it is present in the workspace, and otherwise must be refused (capability null, decline_reason naming the missing deliverable).

A new unit test in outputs.rs reads the generated reading schema and asserts the capability/decline_reason description contains the cite-path-or-commit and refuse rule; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
The reader budget check still passes (reader prompt set within its token budget) and `cargo clippy --workspace` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean; run `cargo test` for the whole workspace.
A decision entry in docs/decisions.md records the call, the alternative of editing reader.md (rejected: token budget), and that the rule is prose-only with no runtime path check.

A reader following the rule on a request that depends on an absent earlier deliverable produces a null capability with a decline_reason naming it; the schema text a reader sees makes this outcome checkable.

out_of_scope: Runtime verification that a cited path or commit exists
Changes to the producer or verifier prompts
